currentContext.business: The Company crushes sugarcane at six sugar plants across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and converts the cane almost fully: sucrose into sugar, molasses/syrup and grain into ethanol and Extra Neutral Alcohol at five distilleries, and bagasse into steam and power used captively and exported to the grid. It sells sugar through institutional and premium channels and markets branded sweeteners (brown sugar, jaggery, low-GI sugar and other premium variants) and staples (rice, pulses, millets) under the 'Parry's' franchise across Southern India, while ethanol is supplied to oil marketing companies under the national blending programme. A nutraceuticals business, including wholly owned US Nutraceuticals Inc., makes organic spirulina, chlorella, carotenoids, astaxanthin and lutein/zeaxanthin largely for export markets.

Co-generation: Bagasse-based steam and power, captive and exported to the grid

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was a consolidation year rather than an expansion year: capital expenditure remained largely moderate and was directed towards routine modernisation and operational efficiency improvements. The main capacity story is the distillery platform, with FY 2025-26 being the second full year of operations at the expanded capacity of 582 KLPD — comprising the 120 KLPD facility at Haliyal, the 45 KLPD expansion at Nellikuppam commissioned in FY 2024-25, and the 120 KLPD multi-feed grain-based facility at Sankili, Andhra Pradesh. The Sankili grain facility operated below optimal utilisation during the year and is still stabilising. Multi-feed capability across Sankili, together with molasses and syrup-based operations at Haliyal, Nellikuppam, Sivagangai and Bagalkot, allows feedstock optimisation as market and policy conditions evolve. In the Consumer Products Group, the Company commissioned its own dal processing facility during the year, strengthening backward integration and enhancing quality control, and expanded its distribution footprint across modern trade, e-commerce platforms and rural and semi-urban markets. The Company is also evaluating expansion of its consumer portfolio through strengthened R&D capabilities and a mix of organic and inorganic growth initiatives. On the divestment side, operations of the wholly owned sugar refinery subsidiary Parry Sugars Refinery India Private Limited (PSRIPL) — an SEZ-based export-oriented refinery unit at Vakalapudi Village, Kakinada — ceased with effect from the close of working hours on March 31, 2026. PSRIPL must now obtain regulatory approvals including from the Development Commissioner, Vishakapatnam Special Economic Zone and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, complete the SEZ exit process, then dismantle and dispose of the entire assets of the Refinery Unit, possibly in one or more tranches depending on commercial feasibility, and surrender the leased land to the lessor. The transaction is at a preliminary stage: purchaser identity, timeline and consideration cannot be determined yet, and disposal is intended to proceed through a competitive bidding / open tender process with proceeds applied to PSRIPL's outstanding liabilities. Shareholder approval for the disposal was sought as a Special Resolution at the Fifty First AGM scheduled for August 12, 2026. Looking forward, management expects capital expenditure to remain controlled, with incremental working capital requirements rather than capex keeping debt levels relatively elevated.

risks.risk: Sugarcane availability — structural decline in cane acreage, especially in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
risks.note: Adverse weather, water scarcity, pest and disease outbreaks and farmers shifting to more remunerative alternative crops may reduce cane availability and hit profitability. The Company has already discontinued operations at Pettavathalai, Pudukkottai and Puducherry; existing units at Nellikuppam, Pugalur, Sivagangai and Sankili remain significantly impacted by declining cane/molasses availability and, if the trend persists, their long-term financial viability may be affected. Management concedes that farmer-engagement, Clean Seed Programme, seaweed-based solutions, mechanised harvesting and R&D initiatives may not fully mitigate the structural risk in these two States.

risks.risk: Raw material pricing — cane price is administered and decoupled from sugar prices
risks.note: Sugarcane prices are determined by the Central and State Governments and are not directly aligned with prevailing sugar prices; any mismatch resulting in unviable cane pricing directly compresses Sugar Division profitability. Mitigation is limited to advocacy through ISMA and SISMA.

risks.risk: Sugar price risk — FRP rises without a corresponding MSP revision
risks.note: Any increase in the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane without a matching increase in the Minimum Support Price for sugar adversely impacts profitability. The Company offsets partially by shifting sales to institutional and retail segments that command a premium over the trade channel and by pushing value-added products such as Amrit and jaggery.

Failure or inadequacy of monsoons, depletion of groundwater levels and deterioration in groundwater quality threaten a water-intensive crop. The Company has adopted advanced water treatment technologies (MWTS, JIVA Water Device) and commenced sensor-based autonomous irrigation to cut consumption and lift productivity.

Non-availability of migrant labour for cane harvesting can delay timely harvesting and hurt overall productivity and recovery. Mitigation relies on local labour, self-harvesting by farmers, mechanised harvesting and wider row planting to enable machine use.

risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk in a cyclical industry
risks.note: Business economics of the integrated sugar industry are significantly influenced by laws and Government policies governing sugarcane and sugar availability, pricing, power tariffs, molasses availability, and ethanol production and sales; stoppage of production due to non-compliance with pollution control regulations, labour laws or other statutory requirements is a further exposure. Financial implication is flagged as negative. Mitigation is the integrated model (sugar + distillery + bagasse-based green energy), value-added products from by-products, business continuity planning, and engagement with Government through industry bodies.

Unsafe practices and an inadequate work environment may create safety risks affecting employee well-being. Mitigation includes behavioural safety capability-building at all levels, a defined maturity roadmap, and a benchmarked Safety Drive with an Action Tracking System, incident reporting, inspections and structured safety observation processes.

risks.risk: Cyber security and IT system availability
risks.note: System unavailability or failure of critical IT systems could disrupt business operations, arising from inadequate processes, cyber security vulnerabilities or insufficient backup and disaster recovery. Mitigation includes reviewed backup and disaster recovery policies, firewalls and SIEM monitoring, and periodic user training and awareness.

one-line thesis: EID Parry executed a strategic exit from the loss-making refinery business (infusing ~Rs 600cr to clear debts) while pivoting CPG towards high-margin sweeteners to fix profitability, though Q4 PAT was severely impacted by refinery closure costs despite operational stability in sugar and ethanol segments.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Mixed (Refinery Rs 1,006cr flat YoY; Sugar Rs 466cr +14% YoY; CPG Rs 115cr -48% YoY due to volume pruning); EBITDA/Margin: Core sugar/co-gen stable, but consolidated PAT distorted by Rs 293cr loss in Refinery segment (vs Rs 99cr loss prior year) driven by closure costs; PAT (rptd): Negative due to one-off refinery write-offs/exit costs; Order Book: N/A (Commodity/FMCG flow business); Net Debt: External borrowing at Rs 593cr; Refinery loans fully paid off via equity infusion.
guidance: Revenue Growth: CPG targeting break-even in 6-8 quarters via premium mix; Margin: CPG aiming for single-digit EBITDA by decade-end; Order Inflow: Ethanol volumes expected to rise to 17cr liters if E30 mandate implemented; Capex/Commissioning: Rs 45cr for new Jaggery facility; Refinery SEZ exit formalities complete by Sep 2026.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for commodity sugar/ethanol; Sales volumes: Sugar 97k MT (+33% YoY), Ethanol/ENA 404 LL, Refinery sales 2.3 LMT.
segment / subsidiary detail: Sugar: Crushed 1.775 MMT cane, 11.19% recovery, realized Rs 39.28/kg; Co-gen: 1,499 LU generated, 845 LU exported @ Rs 4.57/unit; Distillery: 452 LL produced, realization Rs 64.25/L; Refinery: 1.69 LMT produced, 2.3 LMT sold, Rs 293cr loss; CPG: Rs 115cr turnover, strategic shift to browns/premium whites; Nutra: Rs 13cr turnover, Valensa launching prostate/derma products.
growth verticals / optionality: Ethanol blending mandate increase (E20 to E30) driving volume upside; CPG expansion into ethnic snacking and culinary convenience via M&A or organic launches; Premium sweeteners (jaggery, brown sugar) targeting 30%+ gross margins.
margins & cost dynamics: Cane cost rose to Rs 4,087/MT (+Rs 319 YoY) due to FRP hike; CPG margin profile improving as low-margin rice/pulses are defocused; Refinery losses attributed to operating costs during closure phase.
capex / expansion: Rs 45cr allocated for new Jaggery facility; No other major capex planned; Focus on cost efficiency and working capital optimization.
capital allocation: Rs 600cr equity infused to extinguish PSRIPL (Refinery) debt; Future allocation prioritized for CPG brand building, distribution expansion, and marketing mix; No dividends guided until business model strengthens.
risks & watch-items: Global sugar price softening (surplus conditions); Cane availability constraints in Tamil Nadu due to crop competition; Delay in government E30 ethanol mandate implementation; Execution risk in CPG portfolio transformation.
management quality / tone: Pragmatic and defensive on core operations; Decisive on restructuring (refinery exit); Cautiously optimistic on ethanol policy; Non-committal on near-term dividends; Dismissive of takeover speculation.
non-obvious takeaways: Refinery closure funding was entirely equity-backed (Rs 600cr) rather than debt refinancing, cleaning the balance sheet but diluting equity value temporarily; CPG revenue drop of 48% is a deliberate 'quality over quantity' move to fix unit economics, not demand destruction; Power tariff arbitrage benefits from recent tribunal orders are negligible for EID as they sell primarily via exchanges.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company crushes sugarcane at six sugar plants across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and converts the cane almost fully: sucrose into sugar, molasses/syrup and grain into ethanol and Extra Neutral Alcohol at five distilleries, and bagasse into steam and power used captively and exported to the grid. It sells sugar through institutional and premium channels and markets branded sweeteners (brown sugar, jaggery, low-GI sugar and other premium variants) and staples (rice, pulses, millets) under the 'Parry's' franchise across Southern India, while ethanol is supplied to oil marketing companies under the national blending programme. A nutraceuticals business, including wholly owned US Nutraceuticals Inc., makes organic spirulina, chlorella, carotenoids, astaxanthin and lutein/zeaxanthin largely for export markets.

- Parry International FZCO (formerly Parry International DMCC) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of PSRIPL; has ceased operations and is under a voluntary liquidation process under consideration by the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC), Dubai, UAE.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Sugar:** White sugar, Value-added and premium sweetener variants, 'Parry's' branded sugar
- **Distillery:** Ethanol from B-heavy molasses, Ethanol from C-heavy molasses, Ethanol from syrup route, Ethanol from grain route, Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), Industrial alcohol
- **Co-generation:** Bagasse-based steam and power, captive and exported to the grid
- **Consumer Products Group:** Branded retail sugar, Amrit brown sugar, Parry's 'Gold', Jaggery, Low glycaemic index (GI) sugar, Rice, Pulses, Millets
- **Nutraceuticals:** Organic spirulina, Chlorella, Carotenoids, Astaxanthin, Lutein/zeaxanthin

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable for commodity sugar/ethanol; Sales volumes: Sugar 97k MT (+33% YoY), Ethanol/ENA 404 LL, Refinery sales 2.3 LMT.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: CPG targeting break-even in 6-8 quarters via premium mix; Margin: CPG aiming for single-digit EBITDA by decade-end; Order Inflow: Ethanol volumes expected to rise to 17cr liters if E30 mandate implemented; Capex/Commissioning: Rs 45cr for new Jaggery facility; Refinery SEZ exit formalities complete by Sep 2026.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Ethanol blending mandate increase (E20 to E30) driving volume upside; CPG expansion into ethnic snacking and culinary convenience via M&A or organic launches; Premium sweeteners (jaggery, brown sugar) targeting 30%+ gross margins.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Karnataka operations are expected to provide greater stability to the overall sugar business, supported by improved cane availability and favourable climatic conditions
- Cane availability in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh remains a structural challenge from water scarcity, adverse weather, higher cost of cultivation and farmers shifting to alternative crops — expected to continue exerting pressure on those regions
- A revision in the MSP for sugar and an upward adjustment in ethanol procurement prices remain critical to industry profitability; any favourable revision would significantly enhance the earnings potential of both the sugar and distillery segments
- The cost optimisation programme continued during FY 2025-26 and has resulted in significant rationalisation across the manufacturing value chain; benefits are expected to be sustained going forward
- Foray into jaggery is being expanded to capitalise on increasing consumer preference for brown and natural sweeteners as alternatives to refined sugar
- CPG is expected to enter FY 2026-27 on a stronger operational footing after channel correction and receivables clean-up, with tighter credit discipline and strengthened collections improving working capital efficiency
- Corrective and strategic CPG measures taken in FY 2025-26 are expected to translate into improved operational and financial performance from FY 2026-27 onwards
- Financial flexibility from the strategic stake in Coromandel International Limited and the institutional strength of the Murugappa Group supports the transition into a diversified food, nutrition and biofuel enterprise without compromising the credit profile
- Global dietary supplements market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 7% between 2025 and 2030 to around USD 64 billion, with key markets in the United States, China and Western Europe and emerging opportunity in Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa
- Nutraceutical demand themes: gut health, longevity and healthy ageing, vitality, mental well-being, sleep quality, weight management including the impact of GLP-1 therapies, and women's health; green blends are a strategically important category to scale
- Continued growth is expected in the joint health and Astaxanthin segments, projected to outperform other nutraceutical categories in the coming years
- Nutraceuticals margin risk from intense price competition from imports — over 75% of Asian Spirulina products are sourced from China at lower prices — plus US tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty
- Premium positioning in certified organic Spirulina (estimated 17-20% share of the certified organic segment versus roughly 4% of the global Spirulina market by volume) supports differentiation against low-cost alternatives
- Sugar and Distillery together contributed approximately 77% of revenues, Consumer Products around 20%, with Co-generation and Nutraceuticals smaller but strategically important
- Ethanol demand mix shifted in favour of grain-based ethanol while cane ethanol pricing had yet to reflect the evolving demand landscape; industry-wide capacity additions moderated near-term economics for sugar-based ethanol producers
- Rising need for calibrated brand-building, advertising and promotional expenditure in consumer categories could pressure margins during portfolio transition or channel restructuring

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Cane cost rose to Rs 4,087/MT (+Rs 319 YoY) due to FRP hike; CPG margin profile improving as low-margin rice/pulses are defocused; Refinery losses attributed to operating costs during closure phase.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Rs 600cr equity infused to extinguish PSRIPL (Refinery) debt; Future allocation prioritized for CPG brand building, distribution expansion, and marketing mix; No dividends guided until business model strengthens.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was a consolidation year rather than an expansion year: capital expenditure remained largely moderate and was directed towards routine modernisation and operational efficiency improvements. The main capacity story is the distillery platform, with FY 2025-26 being the second full year of operations at the expanded capacity of 582 KLPD — comprising the 120 KLPD facility at Haliyal, the 45 KLPD expansion at Nellikuppam commissioned in FY 2024-25, and the 120 KLPD multi-feed grain-based facility at Sankili, Andhra Pradesh. The Sankili grain facility operated below optimal utilisation during the year and is still stabilising. Multi-feed capability across Sankili, together with molasses and syrup-based operations at Haliyal, Nellikuppam, Sivagangai and Bagalkot, allows feedstock optimisation as market and policy conditions evolve. In the Consumer Products Group, the Company commissioned its own dal processing facility during the year, strengthening backward integration and enhancing quality control, and expanded its distribution footprint across modern trade, e-commerce platforms and rural and semi-urban markets. The Company is also evaluating expansion of its consumer portfolio through strengthened R&D capabilities and a mix of organic and inorganic growth initiatives. On the divestment side, operations of the wholly owned sugar refinery subsidiary Parry Sugars Refinery India Private Limited (PSRIPL) — an SEZ-based export-oriented refinery unit at Vakalapudi Village, Kakinada — ceased with effect from the close of working hours on March 31, 2026. PSRIPL must now obtain regulatory approvals including from the Development Commissioner, Vishakapatnam Special Economic Zone and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, complete the SEZ exit process, then dismantle and dispose of the entire assets of the Refinery Unit, possibly in one or more tranches depending on commercial feasibility, and surrender the leased land to the lessor. The transaction is at a preliminary stage: purchaser identity, timeline and consideration cannot be determined yet, and disposal is intended to proceed through a competitive bidding / open tender process with proceeds applied to PSRIPL's outstanding liabilities. Shareholder approval for the disposal was sought as a Special Resolution at the Fifty First AGM scheduled for August 12, 2026. Looking forward, management expects capital expenditure to remain controlled, with incremental working capital requirements rather than capex keeping debt levels relatively elevated.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Pragmatic and defensive on core operations; Decisive on restructuring (refinery exit); Cautiously optimistic on ethanol policy; Non-committal on near-term dividends; Dismissive of takeover speculation.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "No material litigation is described in the routed sections of the report.", "as_of": "2026-07-17"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated sugarcane model - sugar, distillery and co-generation off the same cane, giving near-complete cane utilisation and a circular, zero-waste energy loop
- Multi-feed distillery flexibility across molasses, syrup and grain feedstocks, described as an important differentiator in navigating volatile input costs and pricing dynamics
- 'Parry's' brand equity in Southern India, with an estimated ~55% share of the branded sweeteners segment
- Strategic 55.58% equity stake in Coromandel International Limited providing financial flexibility and strategic optionality - demonstrated by funding the PSRIPL closure without undue financial strain
- Membership of the Murugappa Group, cited as a source of financial flexibility and strategic strength
- Karnataka operations as a structural strength - crushing rose to 25.64 LMT with recovery at 12.07% versus 11.74%, against structurally challenged Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
- Deep farmer-partnership and agri-tech platform - crop development programmes, the 'Cane Insights' control tower, E-Trip Sheet field-to-factory digital tracking and partnerships with Cultyvate, Jiva and Boomitra securing cane supply
- Short-term credit rating maintained at A1+ for the commercial paper programme, underscoring liquidity strength

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Global sugar price softening (surplus conditions); Cane availability constraints in Tamil Nadu due to crop competition; Delay in government E30 ethanol mandate implementation; Execution risk in CPG portfolio transformation.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Refinery closure funding was entirely equity-backed (Rs 600cr) rather than debt refinancing, cleaning the balance sheet but diluting equity value temporarily; CPG revenue drop of 48% is a deliberate 'quality over quantity' move to fix unit economics, not demand destruction; Power tariff arbitrage benefits from recent tribunal orders are negligible for EID as they sell primarily via exchanges.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Disciplined Renewal — transform the company into a more focused food, nutrition and bioenergy enterprise, prioritising strengthening of existing operations and extracting greater value from past investments over accelerating expansion
- Prune the portfolio to preserve balance sheet strength: exit from the Parry Sugars refinery business after assessing its operational challenges, structural viability and capital intensity, and redeploy capital towards businesses with stronger long-term relevance and return potential
- Project Propel — a targeted initiative to improve cost efficiency and execution …
